claims.summary: Over any field, on the Boolean cube {0,1}^N, let U be an up-set with minimal sets M. The functions given by polynomials of degree <=d vanishing on U have the basis prod_{v in T}(1-x_v) over the transversals T of M (sets meeting every member) with |T|<=d; so their dimension is the number of such transversals and the least degree of a nonzero one is the transversal number tau(M). For a function p, the least degree of such an f with fp nonzero is the least size of a transversal avoiding some point of supp p (infinite if supp p lies in U). Hence for monomial errors c_j x_(A_j), among killers f with deg f+max|A_j|<=D, a common killer modulo the cube's degree-D vanishing ideal that keeps 1 alive exists exactly when tau({A_j})+max|A_j|<=D, of least degree tau({A_j}) (none for a constant error); for Pang's t=1 families over F2 with inputs exactly x_a, x_b and q=x_a+x_b it is the vertex-cover number of the input graph.
claims.assessment: Working proof passed by the sole fresh-context medium reviewer in a staged goal review; the degree window, the Gallai conditions and the relation to the greedy certificate are its corrections.
claims.rationale: Gives the first surviving annihilator degree exactly in the cube's domain model for monomial supports, showing that there every killer is a combination of products of literal killers.
claims.next_action: Test on the hole-respecting domain of the product pigeonhole system, in the inert range and at the top degree, against mixed transversals.
